A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it scrambled, so nobody in between can read it.

Here is how it goes:

Your device scrambles (encrypts) your data and sends it to the VPN company's computer.
That computer unscrambles it and passes it on to the website you asked for.
The website sees the VPN's address, not yours, so your location and identity stay hidden from it.

It helps on public Wi-Fi, since strangers on the same network can't snoop. It also hides your browsing from your internet provider. The VPN company can still see your activity, so pick one you trust. It won't stop viruses or make you anonymous if you sign in to your accounts.
